text:
Alex M.: Heads up — scheduling a targeted maintenance window for AZ-east1 bridge route refresh and a staggered GPU pool drain this Sunday 02:00-05:00 UTC. Goal: apply kernel nvlink fix + cleanly reboot affected racks, avoid cross-region egress spikes.
Maria C.: How many racks/pods are we draining? impact to hosted API and Dedicated?
Alex M.: ~6 racks (priority: batch and hosted burst pools). Expected capacity hit ~18% for AZ-east1 during the window; global impact minimal due to routing. Dedicated pools pinned to customers won't be touched unless explicitly on the affected racks (we'll list tenants).
Rahul P.: Can you put the exact node list? also we should preseed KV caches for common prefixes before drain.
Alex M.: Node list: r-ae-23{1..6} (will paste in infra ticket). Preseed plan: run prefix-warm on top 20 prefixes, seed KV cache using rwctl kv seed --pool=hosted-burst --prefix-file=top20.txt 1h before drain.
SRE Oncall: Add rollback criteria: if tail latency 95p > 200ms for 10min, abort and fallback to alternate region routing. Also set alert for pod restarts > 3/min.
Maria C.: Customer comms? we need copy for status page + support playbook.
Alex M.: Draft comms below — please edit: "Planned network and kernel maintenance in AZ-east1 on Sun 02:00-05:00 UTC. Some hosted requests may route to nearby regions; Dedicated customers on affected racks will be contacted individually. Expect short reconnects but no API-level errors. We will monitor latency and roll back if impact > thresholds."
Rahul P.: Implementation snippet for ops runbook:
```
# drain and reboot sequence (staggered per rack)
for rack in r-ae-231 r-ae-232 r-ae-233 r-ae-234 r-ae-235 r-ae-236; do
  rwctl pool cordon --rack=$rack --reason="kernel-fix"
  rwctl pool drain --rack=$rack --grace=300
  wait-for-empty --rack $rack --timeout 1800
  ssh admin@$rack "sudo /usr/bin/kernel-upgrade && sudo reboot"
  sleep 600  # let KV cache refill and probes stabilize
done
```
Maria C.: Support playbook snippet:
- If customer reports increased latency: check routing -> fallback to region AZ-west2, check tenant pinned pools.
- If errors escalate: escalate to SRE and notify customers with status page update.
SRE Oncall: Make sure the canary rack is r-ae-231. Run canary for 30m, validate 95p latency delta < 30ms and error rate unchanged. If failed: revert route-table and reprovision BGP bridge.
ops-bot: Maintenance created: ID MW-2026-042-az-east1-bridge (scheduled 1965004321 -> 1965015521).
Rahul P.: Cost/throughput note — fallback to cross-region adds egress spend. Estimate: if 5% of traffic routes to AZ-west2 for 3 hours, extra egress ~1.2TB -> ~$90. We recommend informing finance and allocating that to the infra maintenance bucket.
Alex M.: Good call, Rahul. Let's tag cost center INF-MW-420. Also plan to use burst standby racks in AZ-east1 if available to reduce cross-region egress; can we reserve 4 GPUs on standby? @Rahul P. to confirm.
Rahul P.: Confirmed: reserving 4xA100 on standby pool. Will bind to hosted-burst and preseed cache there.
Maria C.: I'll post status page and draft customer email after you share the tenant list. Also will add an internal triage channel #mw-az-east1.
SRE Oncall: I'll create the alert runbook and wire the PagerDuty escalation. Who's owning post-maint health check?
Alex M.: I'll own post-maint checks for first 2 hours (latency/throughput/kv-hit-rate). @SRE Oncall will take over if any anomaly.
Maria C.: All good — please update the infra ticket with exact node IDs and the comms copy.
Alex M.: Will do. TL;DR: Sun 02:00-05:00 UTC, AZ-east1 targeted rack reboots, canary r-ae-231, standby GPUs reserved, KV preseed + rollback thresholds set. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
